Title: Onboarding-trigger result as presented at the May 12, 2023 company all-hands
Event date: May 12, 2023
Presentation: 15-minute talk plus 10-minute Q&A, 2:00–2:25 PM (UTC−05:00)
Audience: The full company all-hands, approximately 140 people
Presenter: Riley Tanaka

Citation-ready account

At the formal May 12, 2023 company all-hands, Riley presented the mid-segment churn investigation—including the onboarding-trigger result—to the full audience of approximately 140 people. The presentation deliberately framed the result as a reusable investigation framework rather than as a postmortem or a victory lap.

The result was presented through a method-first sequence: establish the cohort cut; enumerate the competing hypotheses; show the rule-out cadence; describe the controlled A/B test of `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`; and explain why the team waited for a stabilization cohort before treating the early movement as durable enough to act on. The substantive conclusion was qualified: the onboarding trigger showed a modest positive effect on early/week-1 retention, with the first post-rollout cohort later recorded at +3.2 percentage points versus baseline; the 50–75-seat slice remained noisy, and the result was not presented as proof that the entire mid-segment churn problem was solved.

Recognition recorded in this all-hands presentation

Riley explicitly credited Owen Pham and Ines Kovac by name during the presentation. This note preserves that recognition as a fact about the May 12 all-hands presentation and its contemporaneous record. It is not a universal attribution rule for the onboarding-trigger work, nor does it establish that only those named contributors worked on it. Other records may assign different roles or credit for experiment design, analysis, implementation, review, or rollout.

Presentation context

The framing mattered: Riley kept the emphasis on the investigation method and on the limits of the evidence. In response to questions, Marcus Vail engaged constructively with the presentation, and Tomas asked whether the approach could generalize to other cohorts; Riley endorsed applying the method elsewhere. Those exchanges are part of the event context, not additional contributor credits for the onboarding-trigger result.

Source note

The account above is based on contemporaneous internal records:

[1] May 12, 2023 8:30 AM preparation record: the event was set for a 15-minute talk and 10-minute Q&A; it specifically says to say Owen and Ines out loud and to keep the frame on the framework rather than a postmortem. Session citation: @session:riley-test-118-a01/20261122_232531_d5dd4d.

[2] May 12, 2023 2:00 PM post-event record: Riley reports delivering the full 15 + 10 to the whole approximately 140-person audience, describes the cohort-cut → hypotheses → rule-out cadence → A/B → stabilization sequence, and records Owen Pham and Ines Kovac as named credits. Session citation: @session:riley-test-118-a01/20261122_232556_93ca18.

[3] April 29, 2023 institutional investigation record prepared for circulation and the all-hands: Mid-segment churn investigation Feb-Apr 2023 -- what we learned. It records the experiment key, the modest-positive interpretation, the stabilization-cohort decision, the 100% rollout on April 10, the +3.2 percentage-point first post-rollout read, and the noisy 50–75-seat caveat. Document: https://docs.mock/doc_1795389485071

Archival qualification

This note is an event-specific citation record. It preserves what was said, how the result was framed, the approximate audience scale, and who was explicitly credited in that presentation.
